chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: How High the Moon, Midnight Sun and Fats Navarro
summary: Mingus says he showed Hampton the riffs behind Midnight Sun and was not paid for his charts.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, you were talking about how they swiped -- he and -- is it Johnnie Burke? No, not Johnnie Burke, --
Right, and made it into "Midnight Sun."
I (inaudible) How High the Moon. I showed him the riffs on it. The next thing I know, they had Fats Navarro with him.

(Singing.) (Inaudible) And went back to California. And we had broke him in. He stood in with Milt Jackson, Milt showed him how to lay behind the beat. Hamp could do it, too. close like Milt was showing him. He could play bebop with feeling, And I came to rehearsal one day, early, he was at the piano with Sonny Burke, showing Sonny "How High The Moon", and they were writing -- I didn't know they were writing a tune -- (singing). He got that from FATS NAVARRO -- between me and Milt Jackson and it is Pass The Parcel, is what it is. Fats But I just played the solo. Max showed him the changes, my way.
Did he pay you for all those charts?
You wrote a lot of charts for the band.

No, I didn't get my money. "Mingus (See Insert, p.31) I forgot most of that. There's a bridge to everything on that. Fingers, (inaudible). ^ (Singing.) ^ That's so long ago, I sung it out of tune. Plus, I've forgotten the bridge. (Singing.)
